comment: How scripts/conformance-reports.mjs runs each implementation. Build the adapter first (see its README). env values may use ~ for the home directory. executionArgs are extra kit options for the execution run. notes are hand-written and shown, labelled as such, on the implementation's page.

notes: The differential scripts check graphql-js against the references more broadly than the kit's vectors, and document where it departs from the draft: [lexer and parser](../scripts/differential-lexer.mjs) (`KNOWN`), [validation](../scripts/differential-validation.mjs) (`DISCREPANCIES`), [coercion](../scripts/differential-coercion.mjs) (`KNOWN`) and [type system](../scripts/differential-type-system.mjs) (`VALIDATION_DEVIATIONS`).
Behaviour outside the kit's fixtures is described in the README's [What graphql-js does](../README.md#what-graphql-js-does).

The differential scripts check graphql-js against the references more broadly than the kit's vectors, and document where it departs from the draft: [lexer and parser](../scripts/differential-lexer.mjs) (`KNOWN`), [validation](../scripts/differential-validation.mjs) (`DISCREPANCIES`), [coercion](../scripts/differential-coercion.mjs) (`KNOWN`) and [type system](../scripts/differential-type-system.mjs) (`VALIDATION_DEVIATIONS`).
Behaviour outside the kit's fixtures is described in the README's [What graphql-js does](../README.md#what-graphql-js-does).
The subscription finding is described in the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-java/README.md#known-graphql-java-deviation).
The adapter uses async-graphql's dynamic schema API (`async_graphql::dynamic`). The derive-macro API may behave differently. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/async-graphql/README.md).

The sheet runs the adapter with `--idle`, which claims `idle` by waiting for .NET's thread pool to go quiet: runtime behaviour, not something Hot Chocolate promises. The kit's determinism replay passed, and a run without `--idle` (grace-based, random runs only) found the same failures. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/hotchocolate/README.md).
Both findings are described, with source locations and a standalone reproduction, in the [adapter's README](../adapters/hotchocolate/README.md#known-hot-chocolate-deviations).

The `mutation` finding is graphql-core 3.2's `execute_fields_serially`, which calls every root field's resolver in a plain loop and only chains the awaiting. Resolvers written as `async def` don't start until awaited, so they run in order; resolvers that return a future or task (a DataLoader's `load`, `create_task`) and synchronous resolvers with side effects run early. graphql-core 3.3 chains the calls, as graphql-js does. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-core/README.md).

The sheet runs graphql-ruby with `--invalid-results`: a schema that uses graphql-ruby's documented `type_error` and `rescue_from` hooks. Out of the box, a resolver result of the wrong shape (a non-list for a list, an object for an Int, a runtime type that isn't a possible type, an unknown enum value) raises out of `execute` instead of becoming a field error (§6.4.4), so the client gets no response at all.

The `resultCoercion` finding is graphql-ruby's Int coercion, which calls `to_i`, so `1.2` becomes `1`. Boolean is `!!value`, so `"false"` becomes `true`; the kit doesn't probe Boolean, since §3.5.4 leaves reasonable coercions to the service. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-ruby/README.md).

graphql-go doesn't make runs deterministic (it resolves fields in Go map order), so the adapter doesn't claim `idle` and the kit waits 10 ms after each settle instead; the sheet's cases are random runs only.

The resolver returns a thunk, graphql-go's way to keep several resolvers pending. The Non-Null propagation and mutation ordering findings come from thunks; with `--sync` only the key order, leaf coercion and mutation error findings remain. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-go/README.md#known-graphql-go-deviations).

The adapter uses graphql-dotnet's schema-first `Schema.For`, its default `DocumentExecuter` and the System.Text.Json serializer. List items are `IDataLoaderResult` values, the only kind of item graphql-dotnet waits for. `idle` holds because everything runs on one thread; the determinism replay passed.

The `resultCoercion` finding: `FloatGraphType` passes a non-finite double through, and `GraphQLSerializer` then throws, so the client gets no response. The introspect area grades almost nothing because graphql-dotnet rejects the kit's introspection query (it has no `specifiedByURL`, `isRepeatable` or input-value deprecation). Parse, validate, schema and introspect findings are described with source locations in the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-dotnet/README.md#known-graphql-dotnet-deviations).
